new_findings.text: EU AI Act compliance operationalization is a dominant research focus, with multiple 2025-2026 preprints addressing compliance checkers, machine-readable evidence, and regulatory sandboxes.
new_findings.evidence: Three papers (2025-2026) specifically target EU AI Act implementation: compliance checkers assessment [28], machine-readable compliance evidence via OSCAL [27], and regulatory sandbox operationalization challenges [29].

new_findings.text: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system standard) is being integrated with regulatory exposure frameworks and compliance tooling.
new_findings.evidence: Paper [24] proposes a quantitative ROI framework integrating ISO 42001 and regulatory exposure; paper [27] lists ISO/IEC 42001 alongside EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF as governance frameworks requiring machine-readable evidence.

new_findings.text: NIST AI RMF and OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language) are proposed as technical infrastructure for machine-readable AI compliance evidence.
new_findings.evidence: Paper [27] proposes OSCAL — a NIST standard used for FedRAMP — as interchange format for AI governance, defining 16 property extensions and a three-layer Compliance-as-Code architecture covering policy, evidence, enforcement.

new_findings.text: EU AI Act regulatory sandboxes face a 'triple challenge' of capacity, coordination, and attractiveness to providers.
new_findings.evidence: Paper [29] investigates the AI Act requirement for Member States to establish national AI regulatory sandboxes, identifying capacity constraints, coordination gaps, and low provider attractiveness as key operational hurdles.

new_findings.key: risk-adjusted-roi-frameworks-are-emerging-to-quantify-ai-investments-under-regulatory-uncertainty-integrating-iso-42001
new_findings.text: Risk-adjusted ROI frameworks are emerging to quantify AI investments under regulatory uncertainty, integrating ISO 42001 and regulatory exposure.
new_findings.evidence: Paper [24] presents a financial framework for quantifying AI project returns that explicitly integrates organizational risk profile changes from algorithmic malfunction, adversarial attacks, and regulatory liability, using ISO 42001 as a governance anchor.
